newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bomb threat to Indonesian national car office.
newsitem.headline: Bomb threat to Indonesian national car office.

text.p: An anonymous bomb threat was phoned to the offices of Indonesia's national carmaker on Sunday, but security guards said they found nothing.
The Timor national car is produced by a company headed by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra in conjunction with a South Korean firm.
"We received a call at 8.30 in the morning, saying that four bombs have been planted in the Timor showroom located on the first floor," a security guard said.

The building, Wisma Antara, houses a number of news organisations, including Indonesia's official Antara news agency, Reuters, Japan's Kyodo news agency, the Asian Wall Street Journal and Singapore's Straits Times.

The government has told all state institutions to buy Timor cars and has given the firm special tax breaks. Japan, the United States and the European Union have taken the issue to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on the grounds that it discriminates against other auto makers.
